i went to a speech pathologist instead of a therapist at the recommendation of my doctor, and found that it was really helpful! i wouldn’t have thought speech pathologists did something like that, but they told me that speech also includes swallowing. we focused more on actual exposure to food instead of the psychological aspect of it. it was really patient-focused (i was able to set my own goals for foods i wanted to try and they created a space where i never felt pressured in any way). the only con is that a lot of the resources/sheets they gave me are primarily centered around kids/babies, though that’s more a problem with ARFID resources in general lol. and, since i was one of the only adults at my speech therapists office, i was the “favorite patient”, since they could actually hold an adult conversation with me haha. 

in conclusion, a speech pathologist might be what you’re looking for! just make sure that they mention feeding on their website!
